I am inviting to visit Ladprao 101 road, as it's a very popular place for Songkran celebration with locals and it always a lot of fun! Happy Thai New Year!

snippet.title: The BEST Homestay in Ubon Ratchathani, Thailand | Suan Na Ta Bua Organic Farmstay
snippet.description:
Is community-based and Ecotourism the future of Thai tourism? I found a side of Thailand that 99% of travellers will never see, and it all starts at this incredible organic farmstay in Ubon Ratchathani.

https://suannatabua.com/

Thailand tourism decline is back in the news, so I wanted to look at things from a different angle. This adventure explores the bridge to the REAL Thailand, moving beyond the curated shows to experience the vibrant, unfiltered culture of the Isaan region. I was looking for an answer to the reports of falling tourist numbers, and what I found was a community-funded Morlam concert, a resilient local guide named P'Kek, and a new way forward for tourism.

This video is for anyone tired of the typical travel circuit and looking for a meaningful connection. We explore how a genuine Thailand farmstay or homestay can be the gateway to authentic cultural events you can't find online. From helping out on the organic farm to witnessing a wild, modern Morlam party, this is a look at what happens when you step off the beaten path.

We stayed at the Suan Na Ta Bua (สวนนาต๊ะบัว) organic farmstay in Ubon Ratchathani, Thailand. It's a perfect example of community-based tourism and a must-visit for anyone traveling through the Isaan region.

snippet.title: The REAL Danger of Living in Rural Thailand
snippet.description:
This was filmed with permission. Donations were made to the temple and community. Alcohol is shown only outside temple grounds. I have the deepest respect for the community for allowing me to share this merit-making day. My own flaws are the joke here. I love this place and everyone in it. I am also taking a break from alcohol after making this video.

🇬🇧 ❤️ 🇹🇭

What are the real dangers of living in rural Thailand? When people think about moving to the Land of Smiles, especially to a quiet farm in Isaan, they often worry about snakes, scorpions, or even the notorious Thai roads. While those are valid concerns, this video explores a far more insidious danger, one that's woven into the fabric of the life and greets you with a smile.

Join me on what starts as a perfect day on our homestead, selling fish to the village for a local festival. What begins as a simple transaction quickly spirals into a lack of self-control under the guise of social obligation. This is the story of how quickly the expat dream can be derailed by the powerful culture of social drinking.

We'll look at the subtle pressures, the rationalizations, and the slippery slope from "just one drink" to a full-blown party, a wicked hangover at a sacred temple ceremony, and the realization that you've lost control. This isn't about blaming anyone; it's a personal story about the struggle to find balance when living in a culture so different from your own.

I haven't had a drink since filming this 4 days and I plan to continue for a while.
